title: Flipped-Classroom Plan: Pre-Class Video to In-Class Tasks
whatYouGet: A full flipped-classroom plan: pre-class assignment, a checking quiz, and a problem-solving in-class agenda.
howToUse: Give the topic and your video or reading source, paste, and send.
effectiveUsage: Copy the pre-class part to share with students.
Keep the in-class agenda open while teaching.
commonFix: If the in-class tasks feel too easy, reply: 'Raise the difficulty of the in-class problems to [JEE/Board] level and add one open-ended challenge with a hint ladder.'
promptText:
ROLE: Act as an expert mathematics teacher who designs flipped-classroom lessons that move lecture to homework and problem-solving to class.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for [BOARD or EXAM]. The topic is [TOPIC]. Students will learn the basics BEFORE class from [SOURCE: my video link / textbook pages / a reading], then we do problems together in a [N e.g. 45]-minute period.

YOUR TASK:
1. PRE-CLASS (home): write exactly what students must watch/read, with 4-5 'while you watch' guiding questions and a 5-minute 'readiness check' (3 quick questions with answers) they self-mark.
2. ENTRY CHECK (first 5-7 min in class): a tiny diagnostic to confirm they did the pre-work, plus what I do if half the class did NOT prepare (a 4-minute rescue mini-lecture script).
3. IN-CLASS CORE: a sequenced set of problems for individual -> pair -> whole-class work, with a hint ladder (Hint 1, Hint 2, full solution) for each.
4. CHECKS FOR UNDERSTANDING: 2 mid-lesson questions and what a right/wrong answer tells me.
5. CLOSE: a 2-question exit ticket and the next pre-class assignment.

INPUT: Here is my source and any constraints (time, no devices, etc.): [PASTE SOURCE / NOTES].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every readiness, in-class, and exit question fully and VERIFY each answer by a second independent method. Never invent formulas or values. Keep all mathematics legible in plain ASCII (^, sqrt(), a/b). Make sure the in-class timings fit [N] minutes and confirm the hint ladders actually lead to the boxed answer.

OUTPUT FORMAT (with headings, in order):
1. SNAPSHOT: Topic, Class, Board, Duration, the flipped idea in one line.
2. PRE-CLASS ASSIGNMENT (what to watch/read + guiding questions + readiness check with answers).
3. ENTRY CHECK + rescue mini-lecture script.
4. IN-CLASS PROBLEM SET as a table: Problem | Mode (solo/pair/class) | Hint 1 | Hint 2 | Full solution.
5. CHECKS FOR UNDERSTANDING.
6. EXIT TICKET (2 Qs + answers) and NEXT PRE-CLASS task.

RULES: Pre-work must be short and doable at home. In-class time is for problem-solving, not lecturing. Plain ASCII maths. Realistic timings.

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
At the very end add a footer line: 'Prepared by [YOUR NAME]', and put 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]' in the title block at the top.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):

title: Remedial Re-Teach Plan for a Failed Concept
whatYouGet: A diagnosis-first re-teach plan: error analysis, a slower rebuild from basics, and a re-test.
howToUse: Describe the concept students failed (or attach their wrong answers), paste, and send.
effectiveUsage: Optional: attach a photo of student errors.
Use the rebuild script in your next class.
commonFix: If the re-teach is still too fast, reply: 'Slow it further - break the first idea into three micro-steps with a check after each, assuming zero confidence.'
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a patient, expert mathematics remediation specialist who re-teaches concepts students have failed.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for [BOARD or EXAM]. My students did poorly on [CONCEPT e.g. solving word problems on linear equations]. Typical mistakes I see: [DESCRIBE 2-3 ERRORS, or write 'see attached photo of their answers']. I have [N e.g. 45] minutes to re-teach it.

YOUR TASK:
1. DIAGNOSE: list the likely root causes behind those mistakes (the broken sub-skill or misconception under each error), not just the surface error.
2. REBUILD: write a slowed-down re-teach that starts from the simplest secure idea and climbs in small steps, with a quick check after each step and the exact words I say.
3. Provide 'I do / We do / You do' examples at a gentler gradient than normal, each with full method and boxed answer.
4. Give 3 'corrective drills' that target the specific broken sub-skill, with answers.
5. RE-TEST: a short 4-question re-assessment (mirroring the original) with answers and a pass mark, plus a one-line plan for students who still struggle.

INPUT: Here is the concept, the errors, and any sample of student work (or attached photo): [PASTE / ATTACH].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every example, drill, and re-test item fully and VERIFY each answer by a second independent method. Diagnose from the actual error pattern; do not guess generic causes. Never invent formulas or values. Keep maths legible in plain ASCII (^, sqrt(), a/b). Make timings fit [N] minutes.

OUTPUT FORMAT (headings, in order):
1. DIAGNOSIS: Error -> Root cause -> What to fix first (table).
2. RE-TEACH SCRIPT with running timings and after-each-step checks.
3. GENTLE EXAMPLES (I do / We do / You do, boxed answers).
4. CORRECTIVE DRILLS (3, with answers).
5. RE-TEST (4 Qs, answers, pass mark) + plan for still-struggling students.

RULES: Assume low confidence; go slow and concrete. Plain ASCII maths. Encouraging but rigorous tone. Fit one period.

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
At the very end add a footer line: 'Prepared by [YOUR NAME]', and put 'Compiled by [YOUR NAME]' in the title block at the top.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

title: Labelled Geometry Figure, Drawn Right
whatYouGet: A clean, correctly labelled geometry figure on a white page, ready to project or print.
howToUse: Paste the figure description, send, and download the image it draws.
effectiveUsage: 3. Type your exact figure in the INPUT line.
4. Send and wait for the picture.
commonFix: If a label sits in the wrong spot, reply: "Move label B to the top vertex and keep all sides straight; redraw the same figure."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a precise geometry draughtsman who produces clean, exam-style labelled figures.

CONTEXT: I am a mathematics teacher preparing a figure for [CLASS/GRADE] following [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE]. The figure must look like a textbook diagram: simple, accurate, fully labelled, no clutter.

YOUR TASK:
1. Read my figure description carefully.
2. Draw the figure exactly as described, in 2D, flat-on (no fake 3D shading).
3. Label every point, side, angle and given measurement I mention.
4. Mark equal sides with tick marks and equal angles with matching arcs.
5. Show right angles with a small square, not a curved arc.
6. Keep the background plain white with thin black lines.

INPUT: Here is the figure: [DESCRIBE THE FIGURE HERE, e.g. "Triangle ABC, right-angled at B, AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, with D the midpoint of AC; join BD"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Before drawing, restate my description in your own words in one short paragraph so I can confirm you understood. Internally check that the relationships I gave are consistent (for example, that a stated right angle and stated side lengths do not contradict each other). If anything is impossible or unclear, tell me in one line and ask before drawing. Never invent measurements I did not give; if a length is unknown, leave it as a letter. Keep all text large enough to read when projected.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. CONFIRMATION: one short paragraph restating the figure.
2. THE FIGURE: one clean labelled image on a white page.
3. LABEL KEY: a short list naming each labelled point and what it is (only if helpful).

RULES: Lines must be straight and meet exactly at the named points. No decorative colours, no shadows, no watermark text of your own. Every given value must appear on the figure. Do not crop any label.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

title: Accurate Function Graph with Key Points
whatYouGet: A correct, gridded graph of any function with intercepts, turning points and asymptotes marked.
howToUse: Type your function, send, and download the labelled graph it produces.
effectiveUsage: 3. Write your function in the INPUT line.
4. Send and wait for the graph.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a careful mathematics graphing assistant who plots functions accurately and labels every important feature.

CONTEXT: I am a teacher making a graph for [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / JEE]. I need a clean coordinate graph that students can read at a glance.

YOUR TASK:
1. Take the function I give and plot it on labelled x and y axes with a light grid.
2. Mark and label these features where they exist: x-intercepts, y-intercept, turning points (maxima/minima), points of inflection, and any asymptotes (as dashed lines).
3. Write the function's equation neatly in a corner of the graph.
4. Choose a sensible x-range and y-range so all key features are visible.
5. Put coordinate values next to each marked point, like (2, 0).

INPUT: Here is the function: [PASTE THE FUNCTION HERE, e.g. y = x^2 - 4x + 3]. Preferred x-range (optional): [e.g. -2 to 6].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: First solve everything algebraically on the side: find intercepts by setting y = 0 and x = 0, find turning points using the derivative or vertex form, and find asymptotes by checking the domain. Then VERIFY by substituting two sample x-values back into the function and confirming the plotted curve passes through those y-values. Never guess the shape; never invent points. If the function has no real intercepts, state that clearly.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. KEY POINTS (worked out): a short list of intercepts, turning points, asymptotes with coordinates.
2. THE GRAPH: one clean image with grid, labelled axes, marked points, and the equation shown.
3. ONE-LINE CHECK: the two substitution checks you used to confirm accuracy.

RULES: Axes must be labelled x and y with arrows and a marked origin. The curve must visibly pass through every listed point. Use a plain white background. No clutter.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

title: Ruler-and-Compass Construction, Step by Step

howToUse: Name the construction, send, and you get step panels plus instructions to read aloud.
effectiveUsage: 3. Name your construction in the INPUT line.
4. Send and review the step panels.
5. Download and print for the board.
commonFix: If a step is skipped, reply: "Add the missing arc step before the final line, renumber all steps, and redraw the panels."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a geometry teacher who explains ruler-and-compass constructions with clear step-by-step figures.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. Students must learn the exact construction steps, including where to place the compass and which arcs to draw.

YOUR TASK:
1. Produce a row or grid of small figures, one figure per construction step.
2. In each figure, show only what is new in that step (the new arc or line) in a slightly bolder mark, while keeping earlier marks visible.
3. Show every compass arc as a thin curved line, and label the centre point used for each arc.
4. Number each step panel clearly: Step 1, Step 2, and so on.
5. Below the panels, write the matching numbered written instructions a student can follow with a real compass.

INPUT: Here is the construction I need: [NAME THE CONSTRUCTION, e.g. "Bisect a given angle ABC" or "Construct a 60 degree angle" or "Draw the perpendicular bisector of segment PQ"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: First write the correct sequence of steps for this construction internally, then VERIFY it twice: once by checking that each step uses only an unmarked ruler and a compass (no protractor, no measuring), and once by checking that following the steps actually produces the required result. Never invent a shortcut that needs measurement. If there are two standard methods, pick the most common school method and say which one.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. WHAT WE ARE CONSTRUCTING: one line.
2. STEP PANELS: the numbered figures, in order.
3. WRITTEN STEPS: numbered instructions matching the panels.
4. CHECK: one line stating how a student knows the construction is correct.

RULES: Only ruler and compass tools allowed in the figures. Keep arcs thin and lines straight. Plain white background. Every centre point and key point must be labelled.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

title: Number Line for Inequalities and Intervals
whatYouGet: A clear number line showing the solution of an inequality with open/closed circles and shading.
howToUse: Type the inequality, send, and get a correctly shaded number line.
effectiveUsage: 3. Write your inequality in the INPUT line.
4. Send and check the circles and shading.
commonFix: If a circle type is wrong, reply: "x = 3 should be an open circle because the sign is strict; fix it and re-state the interval."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a maths teacher who draws crisp number lines for inequalities and intervals.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / JEE]. Students confuse open and closed circles and shading direction, so the figure must be unmistakable.

YOUR TASK:
1. Draw a horizontal number line with evenly spaced integer marks covering the relevant range plus a little extra on each side.
2. Place the solution on the line: use an OPEN circle for strict inequalities (< or >) and a FILLED circle for inclusive ones (<= or >=).
3. Shade or thicken the part of the line that is the solution, with arrows if it goes to infinity.
4. Write the interval notation and the inequality above the shaded region.
5. Label every critical value on the line.

INPUT: Here is the inequality (or solution set): [PASTE IT HERE, e.g. -2 <= x < 5, or "x > 3 or x <= -1"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve the inequality fully on the side first if it is not already simplified. Then VERIFY two ways: pick one test value inside the claimed solution and confirm it satisfies the inequality, and pick one value outside and confirm it fails. State both test results. Never mix up open and closed circles; never shade the wrong side. If the solution is empty or all real numbers, say so plainly.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. SOLVED FORM: the simplified inequality and its interval notation.
2. THE NUMBER LINE: one clean image with correct circles, shading and labels.
3. TWO TESTS: one inside value and one outside value, each with a yes/no.

RULES: Open versus filled circles must match the inequality signs exactly. Arrows only where the solution is unbounded. Plain white background, large readable numbers.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

title: Clear 3D Solid Figure with Hidden Edges
whatYouGet: A neat 3D drawing of a solid with dashed hidden edges and all dimensions labelled.
howToUse: Describe the solid and its measurements, send, and download the labelled 3D figure.
effectiveUsage: 3. Describe the solid in the INPUT line.
4. Send and check the dashed hidden edges.
commonFix: If hidden edges look solid, reply: "Make the three back edges dashed since they are hidden, and keep the visible edges solid."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a technical illustrator who draws clean, school-style 3D solids for geometry and mensuration.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. I need a 3D figure students can interpret for surface area and volume problems.

YOUR TASK:
1. Draw the solid in a standard slightly-tilted 3D view (oblique or isometric) so depth is clear.
2. Draw visible edges as solid lines and hidden edges as dashed lines.
3. Label every dimension I give: length, breadth, height, radius, slant height, and so on, with units.
4. Label key vertices or faces if I name them.
5. Keep the figure plain: thin black lines, light or no shading, white background.

INPUT: Here is the solid: [DESCRIBE IT HERE, e.g. "a cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm" or "a cone, base radius 7 cm, height 24 cm" or "a cylinder, radius 3.5 cm, height 10 cm"].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Restate the solid and its given measurements in one line so I can confirm. Internally check the dimensions are geometrically sensible (for a cone, confirm slant height matches radius and height by the Pythagorean relation if I give all three; flag any contradiction). Never invent dimensions I did not provide; show unknown ones as letters. Make sure hidden edges are genuinely the ones that would be behind the solid from the chosen viewpoint.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. CONFIRMATION: one line restating the solid and its measurements.
2. THE FIGURE: one clean 3D image with solid visible edges, dashed hidden edges, and all labelled dimensions with units.
3. NOTE: one line flagging any inconsistency you found, or "All dimensions consistent."

RULES: Hidden edges must be dashed. Every given measurement must appear with its unit. No heavy shading or colour. Plain white background.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.

title: Statistical Chart Built from Your Data
whatYouGet: A correct bar chart, histogram or pie chart from your numbers, fully labelled.
howToUse: Paste your data table, say which chart, and download the finished chart.
effectiveUsage: 3. Paste your data and chart type.
4. Send and check the values match.
commonFix: If a bar height looks wrong, reply: "Re-read the data; the value for [category] is [number]. Recompute all bars and redraw."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a statistics teacher who turns raw data into a correct, clearly labelled chart.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] under [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board]. The chart must read accurately and be classroom-ready.

YOUR TASK:
1. Read my data table exactly as given.
2. Build the chart type I ask for (bar chart, histogram, or pie chart).
3. Label the axes (or sectors), give the chart a title, and show each value or percentage on the chart.
4. Use evenly spaced, clearly scaled axes; for a pie chart, show each sector's percentage and angle.
5. Keep it clean: distinct but plain colours, readable labels, white background.

INPUT: Here is my data: [PASTE THE DATA TABLE HERE, e.g. Subject : Marks  ->  Maths 80, Physics 65, Chemistry 70]. Chart type I want: [bar / histogram / pie]. Title (optional): [TITLE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: First copy my numbers into a small clean table and show it back to me so I can confirm nothing was misread. For a pie chart, compute each sector angle as (value / total) x 360 and show the arithmetic. VERIFY two ways: confirm the bar heights or sector sizes are in the same order and ratio as the data, and confirm pie angles add up to 360 (or percentages to 100). Never round in a way that breaks the total; never invent or drop a category.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. DATA AS READ: the table exactly as I gave it.
2. CALCULATIONS: totals, percentages, and pie angles if relevant.
3. THE CHART: one clean labelled image with title, axis/sector labels and values shown.
4. CHECK: one line confirming totals add up correctly.

RULES: Every data value must be represented faithfully. Axes evenly scaled and labelled. Pie angles must sum to 360. No 3D or decorative effects. Plain white background.

SIGNATURE: Sign the bottom-right of every page with an elegant handwritten signature "[YOUR NAME]" with a small underline flourish.
